items.q: Why does 'how's your battery?' beat 'how are you?'
items.a: Brenda's kids answered **'fine'** to how are you, and a **percentage plus a need** to how's your battery (snack, decompress). Ko ran with it because it is simple and **does not charge the room** the way 'mental health' still does. Zero and 100 are easy; daily life lives in the middle.

items.q: What are the four battery zones?
items.a: **75–100** keep moving. **50–75** start planning a recharge. **25–50** take a break (walk, phone down, stop the Zoom litany). **0–25** hard stop. Below 50% Ko's work is **embarrassingly bad**, and **no amount of AI** fixes it.

items.q: What is the difference between rest and recharge?
items.a: **Rest** feels like stealing time. **Recharge** is how tomorrow gets a present person. Shetty cancelled dinner after an 8:30am–9:30pm shoot so he could show up for two interviews. Setpoints differ: Ko cannot take an EV to 5%.

items.q: What is the difference between good stress and bad stress at work?
items.a: Checking 'are you done / why didn't numbers triple' makes people work **harder**. The right amount (**eustress**) makes them work **better**. 24/7 pile-on becomes anxiety, depression, physical illness. A still mind is **faster**, not slower.

items.q: What does Ko replace 'just power through' with?
items.a: **Power up.** His Korean mother said power through when he had unnamed test/speaking anxiety at 14. **61%** feel expected to just get over stress; **33%** are too overwhelmed to think ahead.

items.q: When should you name your chargers?
items.a: **While you are still at 70%.** Sleep, mindfulness, food, workout, and loved people are different chargers. Deciding at 5% makes you more overwhelmed. Pre-stage → breath work; late nights → only sleep; busy week → no social plans.

items.q: What happened to Shetty's battery in the room, and what is the claim?
items.a: He came in at **~60** after Diwali social load and left at **~95**. **Presence charges both people.** Open tabs drain. Do not ask how someone is if you cannot stay for a 5% answer. Ko: 'You never asked me how my battery is.'
